blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Port Moody total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Listings of condos and townhomes in North Shore (Port Moody) rose from 35 in June to 43 in September (+22.9%), and 23 sold across the 4 months. In September the community held 22.4% of Port Moody’s 192 condos and townhomes listed.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in North Shore (Port Moody)?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 43 condos and townhomes listed in North Shore (Port Moody). That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is North Shore (Port Moody) a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in North Shore (Port Moody) had a sales ratio of 16%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in North Shore (Port Moody) from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 23 condos and townhomes sold in North Shore (Port Moody) over those 4 months, out of 141 in all of Port Moody.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.
